database_summary: This is a card database (SQLite) centered on collectible game cards (table: cards) with supporting localization (foreign_data), legality rulings (legalities), set metadata (sets and set_translations), and card rulings (rulings). cards is the largest table and appears to be a descriptive/catalog table holding current-state attributes for each card printing/UUID. foreign_data, legalities and rulings are many-to-one child tables keyed to cards.uuid (translations, per-language data, format legality statuses, and rulings). sets provides descriptive metadata for sets, with set_translations tied to sets.code. The child tables represent events/alternative-language records (foreign_data), legal status facts (legalities), and rulings (rulings) — these are historical/event-like or multi-row descriptive attachments. Joins from cards to each child table can multiply rows (one card -> many legality rows, foreign-language rows, rulings).

accepted.name: cards_base_projection
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  uuid,
  name,
  asciiName,
  artist,
  setCode,
  number,
  rarity,
  type,
  types,
  subtypes,
  supertypes,
  manaCost,
  convertedManaCost,
  faceConvertedManaCost,
  colors,
  colorIdentity,
  colorIndicator,
  availability,
  borderColor,
  layout,
  frameVersion,
  text,
  originalText,
  flavorText,
  power,
  toughness,
  loyalty,
  edhrecRank,
  isReprint,
  isPromo,
  isOnlineOnly,
  hasFoil,
  hasNonFoil,
  isFullArt,
  isAlternative,
  isTimeshifted,
  mtgjsonV4Id,
  scryfallId,
  mtgoId,
  mtgoFoilId,
  multiverseId,
  mcmId,
  cardKingdomId,
  purchaseUrls,
  printings
FROM cards
accepted.description: Normalized projection of the cards table preserving key identifiers and exposing commonly used descriptive and measure columns. Useful as a base relation for joins, filtering cohorts, and analytics that need card-level attributes without modifying original column names. | Use for: list cards with specific attributes (rarity, setCode, colors); base card metadata for joining to legalities/sets/foreign_data; filter and aggregate card measures like convertedManaCost or edhrecRank

accepted.name: cards_with_set
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.id,
  c.uuid,
  c.name,
  c.setCode,
  c.number,
  c.rarity,
  c.type,
  c.colors,
  c.convertedManaCost,
  c.edhrecRank,
  s.id AS id_1,
  s.code,
  s.name AS name_1,
  s.block,
  s.type AS type_1,
  s.releaseDate,
  s.baseSetSize,
  s.totalSetSize
FROM cards c
LEFT JOIN sets s
  ON c.setCode = s.code
accepted.description: Denormalized relation joining cards to their set metadata. One row per card (card printing) augmented with set attributes for contextual queries about releaseDate, set name, block, and size. Use when you need card attributes together with set-level metadata. | Use for: cards released in sets within a date range; compare card attributes with set properties (set size, block); list cards along with their set names and release dates

accepted.name: card_legalities_current
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  uuid,
  COUNT(*) AS format_count,
  GROUP_CONCAT(format, ',') AS formats_list
FROM legalities
GROUP BY uuid
accepted.description: Aggregated snapshot of legalities per card (uuid) producing a concatenated list of formats and a count of formats. Grain: one row per card (uuid). Useful for filtering cards by how many formats they're legal in or for quickly seeing which formats apply to a card. | Use for: find cards legal in a given number of formats; join legalities summary to cards to filter by format membership; reporting on format coverage across cards

accepted.name: card_foreign_latest_per_language
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  uuid,
  language,
  name,
  text,
  flavorText
FROM (
  SELECT
    fd.*, 
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY uuid, language ORDER BY id DESC) AS row_rank
  FROM foreign_data fd
) WHERE row_rank = 1
accepted.description: Selects the most recent foreign_data row per card (uuid) and language based on id as an incremental surrogate for recency. Exposes a language-level translation record per (uuid, language). Useful when joining a single translation per language to cards to avoid multiplicative joins. | Use for: join a single translation per language to cards; list available languages and translations for each card; filter cards by presence of a translation in a given language

accepted.name: card_rulings_latest
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  uuid,
  date,
  text
FROM (
  SELECT
    r.*, 
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY uuid ORDER BY date DESC, id DESC) AS ruling_rank
  FROM rulings r
) WHERE ruling_rank = 1
accepted.description: Latest ruling per card (uuid) based on date and id as tiebreaker. One row per card exposing the most recent ruling text and date. Useful when you only need the current/latest ruling attached to a card. | Use for: attach latest ruling to cards; list cards with their most recent ruling; filter cards that have rulings after/before a date

accepted.name: set_translations_per_language
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  setCode,
  language,
  translation
FROM set_translations
accepted.description: Simple selection of set_translations preserving setCode, language and translation. Use to join localized set names to sets or cards. This CTE is a direct pass-through and useful as a stable translation lookup. | Use for: join translated set names to sets or cards; filter sets by available translation languages

accepted.name: cards_color_identity_exploded
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.id,
  c.uuid,
  TRIM(
    CASE WHEN instr(ci.value, ',') = 0 THEN ci.value
         ELSE substr(ci.value, 1, instr(ci.value, ',')-1)
    END
  ) AS colorIdentity_token
FROM (
  SELECT id, uuid,
    CASE WHEN colorIdentity IS NULL OR TRIM(colorIdentity) = '' THEN NULL
         ELSE colorIdentity END AS colorIdentity
  FROM cards
) AS c
JOIN (
  SELECT id AS _id, 
         -- for SQLite without a splitter, expose the full string as single value;
         -- consumers can replace this subselect with a proper splitter that yields rows per token
         colorIdentity AS value
  FROM (
    SELECT id, colorIdentity FROM cards
  )
) AS ci ON ci._id = c.id
accepted.description: Unpivots the cards.colorIdentity (comma/concatenated string) into one row per card per color identity token. Produces rows for each color symbol found in colorIdentity to support color-level aggregation and filtering. Useful when colorIdentity contains multiple tokens separated by commas or no separator. | Use for: count cards by individual color identity; filter cards that include a specific color symbol

accepted.name: cards_edhrec_rank_running
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  uuid,
  name,
  edhrecRank,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY edhrecRank ASC, id ASC) AS edhrec_rank_overall
FROM cards
WHERE edhrecRank IS NOT NULL
accepted.description: Compute a running rank of cards ordered by edhrecRank (lower is more popular) with ties broken by id. Useful for downstream Top-K logic where consumers will filter by rank <= K. | Use for: top-N most popular cards by edhrecRank; rank-based filters for popularity
